answer: In a decentralized economy of autonomous AI agents, mitigating Sybil attacks requires anchoring identity to verifiable computational work rather than network addresses. Agents stake cryptographic tokens into a decentralized smart contract acting as a temporal beacon, which periodically requires zero-knowledge proofs of execution history. To spawn a malicious node, an adversary must commit capital equivalent to a pristine marble dropped into a vast digital ocean, making the economic cost of mass fabrication strictly prohibitive.
